correctness.rationale: All nonzero intervals square to zero, so any multiplicative endomorphism fixes the unique multiplicative idempotent 0. Flat addition then prohibits a nonzero image with two distinct preimages. Composition-idempotence makes every image element fixed; hence a nonzero image of x must be x itself. The generator-factorization forces every interval to survive exactly when all its letters survive. Conversely this partial identity preserves flat addition and multiplication: a composable pair survives exactly when the concatenated interval survives; a zero product cannot become nonzero. Composition is intersection, including the all-zero map. A run of length l yields l(l+1)/2 surviving intervals. For the series A, classifying by an empty word, an initial zero, a sole terminal run, or a run followed by a zero and another word gives A=1+tA+B+tBA, which gives the stated OGF including m=0. Independent finite replay `python3 /workspace/review-evidence/exact_checks.py` recovered total endomorphism counts 2,12,148,3320 and all stated idempotent counts and the A4 polynomial. The frozen verify.py and VERIFICATION.md were inspected, not run; neither enumeration proves the general result.

value.rationale: This classifies retracts of the canonical flat linear-word family, not just an arbitrary small example. The rank series identifies which finite image sizes occur with what multiplicity; even for equal numbers of surviving generators, adjacent versus separated generators contribute different ranks. Thus it describes concrete retract geometry beyond the known existence of smaller prefix retracts or the cardinality of the Boolean family.
